claims.text: Severe cryo-rolling followed by annealing can tailor a heterogeneous microstructure and overcome the strength-ductility trade-off.
The investigated alloy is CoCrFeNi2.1Nb0.2.
The initial microstructure consists of an FCC matrix containing complex Laves-phase particles.

The processing schedule comprised homogenization at 1200 °C for 24 h, rolling to 90% thickness reduction, liquid-nitrogen immersion for 0.5 h before and after each cryo-rolling pass, annealing at 800 °C for 1 h, and water quenching.
Cryo-rolling followed by annealing produces a heterogeneous microstructure containing coexisting deformed and recrystallized regions.
The cryo-rolled alloy has a greater density of precipitation nucleation sites, including dislocations, shear bands, and grain boundaries.
The greater nucleation-site density accelerates precipitation of nanosized ε phase early in recrystallization.
The nanosized ε precipitates pin high-angle boundaries through Zener pinning.
Boundary pinning inhibits recrystallization and thereby preserves a mixture of deformed and recrystallized regions.
Mechanical incompatibility between deformed and recrystallized regions generates strain gradients and geometrically necessary dislocations.
The geometrically necessary dislocations create long-range back stress that delays necking.
The back-stress mechanism enhances both strength and ductility.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has a yield strength of 1219 ± 14 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has an ultimate tensile strength of 1272 ± 25 MPa.
The cryo-rolled and annealed alloy has approximately 22% elongation.
The cold-rolled and annealed baseline has a yield strength of 774 ± 13 MPa.
The cold-rolled and annealed baseline has an ultimate tensile strength of 1085 ± 18 MPa.
The cold-rolled and annealed baseline has approximately 20% elongation.
Cryo-rolling and annealing increase yield strength by approximately 400 MPa, or approximately 58%, relative to cold-rolling and annealing.
The study did not quantify the back stress generated by the heterogeneous microstructure.
